newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends up on technically-driven buying.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends up on technically-driven buying.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures closed a heavily-traded session firmer as market sources grappled for a fundamental reason behind today's move.
Fund buying and a lack of selling interest buoyed the December contract over support at 78.00, but the contract slipped back on the close.
"We were down for four days and this is the second day up, so this may be more technical," said Sharon Johnson, an analyst with Frank Schneider and Co Inc.
Trade selling came in around 77.00 cents in December. A dealer also cited buy stops above 77.90.
December settled up 1.59 at 77.75, having ranged from 78.10 to 76.55. The back months finished 1.54 to 0.72 higher.
Despite concerns of moisture in parts of Texas and the Delta, and near-freezing temperatures in CIS states, forecasts were not drastic enough to spark today's gains.
"It doesn't matter if the rain ruins the crop. The charts look bullish and the rain is an added reason to buy," a Texas-based trader said.
And while the weather may have prompted some renewed concern over the U.S. crop, "what does it matter if there's no demand?," said Johnson, referring to slack exports and strong imports.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture will release its latest weekly export figures Thursday, and its monthly supply and demand estimates October 11.
